findings.title: No regression test for the ISR path-restore branch
findings.why_it_matters:
This PR fixes a regression where every ISR route returned 404, and that regression shipped because no test ran the built _isr function with the rewritten `/_isr?x_astro_path=` request. The existing suites still cannot catch it: isr.test.js only checks the generated config JSON, and path-override-security.test.js only checks that overrides are rejected. If someone tightens the override gate again, every ISR page will 404 while CI stays green. An in-process probe shows the test is cheap. The built fixtures/isr _isr function returns 404 without `x-vercel-isr: 1` and returns 200 `

One

` with the header. A test that asserts this pins the contract this PR restores.
findings.suggested_fix:
In test/isr.test.js, add a case that reuses the loadFunctionModule helper from path-override-security.test.js (or moves it into test-utils.js) to load the `_isr` function. Call `fetch(new Request('https://example.com/_isr?x_astro_path=/one', { headers: { 'x-vercel-isr': '1' } }))` and assert status 200 and that the body contains `

One

`. Assumption: the fixture's one.astro stays the ISR page covered by the `^/one/?$ -> /_isr?x_astro_path=$0` route.
evidence: test/isr.test.js only asserts _isr.prerender-config.json and config.json routes; it never invokes a built function

Probe (tmp/isr-probe2.mjs, built fixtures/isr _isr.func): no header -> 404 Not Found; {'x-vercel-isr':'1'} -> 200

One
provenance: 335a20416 Require trusted secret for path overrides (#15959) introduced the ISR regression and its tests all passed; the fix 71ae51338 adds no test

findings.title: Security suite has no case for spoofed x-vercel-isr header
findings.why_it_matters: The new branch lets anyone who sends `x-vercel-isr: 1` override the rendered path. _isr and _render use the same handler (identical `.vc-config.json` handler `dist/server/entry.mjs`), so the handler cannot tell whether it runs as the ISR function. When the built _render function gets `/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private` with `x-vercel-isr: 1`, it currently returns `{"id":"private"}`. Without the header it returns `public`. path-override-security.test.js only covers the no-header case, so it still passes even though the boundary #15959 closed is open again for any client that can set this header. Whether Vercel strips a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` is a platform guarantee that neither the code nor the tests pin down. A negative test would force that decision into the code, for example by also requiring the `/_isr` pathname or another server-only signal.
findings.suggested_fix: In test/path-override-security.test.js, add `it('ignores x_astro_path on _render even with x-vercel-isr header')`. It sends `new Request('https://example.com/api/public?x_astro_path=/api/private', { headers: { 'x-vercel-isr': '1' } })` to the _render function and asserts `body.id === 'public'`. To make it pass, narrow the gate in entrypoint.ts to honor the query param only when `url.pathname === '/_isr'` and `x-vercel-isr === '1'`. Assumption: Vercel invokes the ISR function at the `/_isr` path produced by ISR_PATH. If the maintainers conclude Vercel guarantees the header cannot be spoofed, keep the test but document that platform dependency in a comment beside the branch.
evidence: Probe (tmp/isr-probe.mjs, built serverless-with-dynamic-routes _render.func): no header -> 200 {"id":"public"}; x-vercel-isr: 1 -> 200 {"id":"private"}

residual_risks: Real Vercel platform behavior can't be tested offline: whether the edge or firewall strips or overwrites a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` header on requests to _render or _isr. The in-process probes cover only the handler logic.
